subject: Educational Freedom and Curricular Inclusivity
overview: School Committee Member Aaron Olapade delivered an address for the National Day of Action, framing the defense of inclusive education as a continuation of Congressman John Lewis's legacy. He advocated for honest history in classrooms and the protection of diverse student identities against national trends of censorship.

items.title: National Day of Action Address
items.summary: Olapade honored the legacy of Congressman John Lewis and called for a commitment to social justice and conscience.

items.title: Education and Censorship
items.summary: The speaker addressed national efforts to ban books and silence discussions regarding race, gender, and sexuality in public schools.

items.title: School Committee Responsibility
items.summary: Olapade emphasized the role of local school boards as a defense against sanitized history and advocated for curricula that include Black, indigenous, and queer voices.

items.title: Advocacy for Inclusive Schools
items.summary: The speaker called for equitable funding and culturally responsive teaching to ensure schools remain brave spaces for all students.

items.title: Call to Action
items.summary: The address concluded with a call to organize against injustice in educational spaces and continue the fight for truth and representation.
